topic: Fabius Gurges defeats the Samnites aided by his father Fabius Maximus as legate
quote_la: cum pater ei Fabius Maximus legatus datus fuisset, et Samnitas vicit et plurima ipsorum oppida cepit

topic: Curius Dentatus and Cornelius Rufinus crush the Samnites, ending the Samnite wars
quote_la: P. Cornelius Rufinus M. Curius Dentatus, ambo consules, contra Samnitas missi ingentibus proeliis eos confecere

topic: War declared on Tarentum for outraging Roman envoys; Pyrrhus summoned to Italy
quote_la: Tarentinis, qui iam in ultima Italia sunt, bellum indictum est, quia legatis Romanorum iniuriam fecissent

topic: Tarentines insult the Roman embassy, causing the Tarentine war
quote_la: Aderat sine mora querelam ferens legatio: hanc quoque foede per obscenam turpemque dictu contumeliam violant; et hinc bellum

topic: Pyrrhus defeats Laevinus at Heraclea by the terror of his elephants
quote_la: Commissa mox pugna, cum iam Pyrrus fugeret, elephantorum auxilio vicit, quos incognitos Romani expaverunt

topic: First battle against Pyrrhus under the consul Laevinus at Heraclea
quote_la: Apud Heracleam Campaniae fluviumque Lirim Laevino consule prima pugna

topic: Curius Dentatus defeats Pyrrhus returned from Sicily and drives him from Italy
quote_la: Curius contra eum pugnavit, exercitum eius cecidit, ipsum Tarentum fugavit, castra cepit

topic: Alliance concluded with Ptolemy king of Egypt
quote_la: legati Alexandrini a Ptolomaeo missi Romam venere et a Romanis amicitiam, quam petierant, obtinuerunt

topic: Colonies founded at Ariminum and Beneventum after the Picentes are defeated
quote_la: Conditae a Romanis civitates Ariminum in Gallia et Beneventum in Samnio

topic: The Sallentini subdued and Brundisium captured
quote_la: Sallentinis in Apulia bellum indictum est, captique sunt cum civitate simul Brundisini

topic: The Picentes and their capital Asculum subdued
quote_la: Domiti ergo Picentes et caput gentis Asculum Sempronio duce

topic: The First Punic War begins under Appius Claudius
quote_la: Et contra Afros bellum susceptum est primum Ap. Claudio Q. Fulvio consulibus

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XVIII (Bellum Punicum primum)
topic: Appius Claudius crosses the strait and swiftly defeats Hiero of Syracuse
quote_la: statimque ac sine mora Hieronem Syracusanum tanta celeritate devicit, ut ille se prius victum quam hostem videret fateretur

topic: Cornelius Asina captured by Punic fraud; Duilius wins Rome's first naval victory
quote_la: Consul Cornelius fraude deceptus est. Duillius commisso proelio Carthaginiensium ducem vicit, triginta et unam naves cepit

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XVIII (Bellum Punicum primum)
topic: Duilius triumphs after the naval victory off the Liparae islands
quote_la: Victor ergo apud Liparas mersa aut fugata hostium classe primum illum maritimum egit triumphum

topic: Regulus defeated and captured in Africa by the Spartan Xanthippus
quote_la: Et duce Xanthippo, qui a Lacedaemoniis missus fuerat, Romanorum dux Regulus victus est ultima pernicie

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XVIII (Bellum Punicum primum)
topic: Regulus' army battles the monstrous serpent at the river Bagradas
quote_la: mirae magnitudinis serpens posita apud Bagradam castra vexaverit

topic: Regulus, sent to Rome on parole, dissuades the senate from peace
quote_la: dixitque se ex illa die, qua in potestatem Afrorum venisset, Romanum esse desisse

topic: Metellus defeats the Punic elephants in Sicily and parades them in triumph
quote_la: Metellus in Sicilia Afrorum ducem cum centum triginta elephantis et magnis copiis venientem superavit

topic: Claudius Pulcher fights against the auspices and is defeated at sea
quote_la: Claudius contra auspicia pugnavit et a Carthaginiensibus victus est

topic: Lutatius Catulus wins the final naval battle and Carthage sues for peace
quote_la: anno belli Punici vicesimo et tertio Catulo bellum contra Afros commissum est

topic: The rebellious Falisci subdued within six days
quote_la: Quod ambo consules intra sex dies, quam venerant, transegerunt

topic: Marcellus kills the Insubrian chief and wins the spolia opima
quote_la: occiso enim rege Marcellus tertia post Romulum patrem Feretrio Iovi opima suspendit

topic: Illyrian war declared after Queen Teuta's murder of Roman envoys
quote_la: Legatos quippe nostros, ob ea quae deliquerant iure agentes, ne gladio quidem, sed ut victimas securi percutiut

topic: Marcius Figulus' earlier Dalmatian campaign at Delminium recalled
quote_la: Hos iam pridem Marcius consul incerta urbe Delminio quasi detruncaverat

topic: Mummius and then Marcellus campaign successfully in Spain
quote_la: Insequenti anno L. Memmius in Lusitania bene pugnavit. Marcellus postea consul res ibidem prosperas gessit

topic: The Third Punic War begins in the 602nd year of the city
quote_la: Tertium deinde bellum contra Carthaginem suscipitur, sexcentesimo et altero ab urbe condita anno

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXI (Bellum Punicum tertium)
topic: Cato urges the destruction of Carthage against Scipio Nasica's dissent
quote_la: Cato inexpiabili odio delendam esse Carthaginem, et cum de alio consuleretur, pronuntiabat, Scipio Nasica servandam

topic: Death of Masinissa, Rome's ally, in extreme old age
quote_la: Masinissa, rex Numidarum, per annos sexaginta fere amicus populi Romani, anno vitae nonagesimo septimo mortuus

topic: Metellus crushes the pretender Pseudophilippus and recovers Macedonia
quote_la: Q. Caecilius Metellus dux a Romanis contra Pseudophilippum missus est et XXV milibus eius occisis Macedoniam recepit

topic: Scipio captures and destroys Carthage in its 700th year
quote_la: Ita Carthago septingentesimo anno, quam condita erat, deleta est

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXI (Bellum Punicum tertium)
topic: Hasdrubal's wife hurls herself with her children into burning Carthage
quote_la: Quae comprehensis duobus liberis a culmine se domus in medium misit incendium, imitata reginam quae Carthaginem condidit

topic: Mummius captures and destroys Corinth after the insult to Roman envoys
quote_la: Corinthiis quoque bellum indictum est, nobilissimae Graeciae civitati, propter iniuriam legatorum Romanorum. Hanc Mummius consul cepit et diruit

topic: Mummius routs Diaeus' Achaean army at the Isthmus
quote_la: Hic alterius ducis Diaei late exercitum sub ipsis Isthmi faucibus fudit geminosque portus sanguine infecit

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXIII (Res in Hispania gestae)
topic: Viriathus rises from hunter to brigand to commander in Lusitania
quote_la: qui ex venatore latro, ex latrone subito dux atque imperator et, si fortuna cessisset, Hispaniae Romulus

topic: The second pretender (Pseudoperses) crushed by the quaestor Tremellius
quote_la: collectis servitiis rebellavit et, cum sedecim milia armatorum haberet, a Tremellio quaestore superatus est

topic: Viriathus murdered by his own men after fourteen years of war
quote_la: Quo metu Viriathus a suis interfectus est, cum quattuordecim annis Hispanias adversus Romanos movisset

topic: Q. Pompeius makes an ignoble peace with Numantia
quote_la: Q. Pompeius deinde consul, a Numantinis, quae Hispaniae civitas fuit opulentissima, superatus, pacem ignobilem fecit

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXIII (Res in Hispania gestae)
topic: Viriathus killed by treachery and hired assassins
quote_la: fractum ducem et extrema deditionis agitantem per fraudem et insidias et domesticos percussores adgressus

topic: Mancinus concludes the infamous peace with the Numantines
quote_la: Post eum C. Hostilius Mancinus consul iterum cum Numantinis pacem fecit infamem

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXIII (Res in Hispania gestae)
topic: Decimus Brutus conquers Gallaecia and crosses the dreaded river of Oblivion
quote_la: Decimus Brutus aliquando latius Celticos Lusitanosque et omnis Gallaeciae populus formidatumque militibus flumen Oblivionis

topic: Senate voids Mancinus' treaty and orders him handed over to the enemy
quote_la: quam populus et senatus iussit infringi atque ipsum Mancinum hostibus tradi

topic: Rome expiates the disgrace of the treaty by surrendering Mancinus
quote_la: populus Romanus dedecus quidem praesentis flagitii deditione Mancini expiavit

topic: Brutus triumphs over the Callaeci and Lusitani
quote_la: D. Iunius Brutus de Callaecis et Lusitanis magna gloria triumphavit

topic: Scipio restores discipline in the demoralized army before Numantia
quote_la: Is primum militem vitiosum et ignavum exercendo magis quam puniendo sine aliqua acerbitate correxit

topic: Scipio expels prostitutes, sutlers and baggage from the camp
quote_la: Ad hoc scorta, calones, sarcinae nisi ad usum necessariae amputantur

locus_hint: liber II, cap. II (Seditio Tiberi Gracchi)
topic: Tiberius Gracchus kindles the first torch of civil strife
quote_la: Primam certaminum facem Ti. Gracchus accendit, genere, forma, eloquentia facile princeps

topic: Attalus of Pergamum dies leaving the Roman people his heir
quote_la: Eodem tempore Attalus, rex Asiae, frater Eumenis, mortuus est heredemque populum Romanum reliquit

topic: Scipio starves Numantia into surrender and razes it
quote_la: postremo ipsam Numantiam diu obsessam fame confecit et a solo evertit

topic: Crassus defeated and killed fighting Aristonicus in Asia
quote_la: Victus est tamen Crassus et in proelio interfectus est. Caput ipsius Aristonico oblatum est

topic: Aristonicus seizes Asian cities and destroys Crassus' army
quote_la: Crassi quoque praetoris cecidit exercitum ipsumque cepit

topic: War beyond the Alps against the Salluvii to protect Massilia
quote_la: Prima trans Alpes arma nostra sensere Saluvii, cum de incursionibus eorum fidissima atque amicissima civitas Massilia quereretur

topic: Metellus subdues the pirate Balearic islanders and earns his cognomen
quote_la: altero et liberis eius Cretico facto mora non fuit quin alter quoque Balearicus vocaretur

locus_hint: liber II, cap. III (Seditio C. Gracchi)
topic: Gaius Gracchus takes up his brother's laws as tribune
quote_la: Statim et mortis et legum fratris sui vindex non minore impetu incaluit C. Gracchus

locus_hint: liber II, cap. III (Seditio C. Gracchi)
topic: Gaius Gracchus overwhelmed on the Aventine by the consul Opimius
quote_la: inde quoque obvia senatus manu ab Opimio consule oppressus est

topic: The Arverni and their king Bituitus crushed near the Rhone
quote_la: Arvernorum tunc nobilissimae civitati atque eorum duci Bituito infinitamque multitudinem iuxta Rhodanum fluvium interfecerunt

topic: King Bituitus displayed in his silver chariot in the triumph
quote_la: Nihil tam conspicuum in triumpho quam rex ipse Bituitus discoloribus in armis argenteoque carpento, qualis pugnaverat

topic: Metellus' Dalmatian victory and triumph
quote_la: a L. Caecilio Metello et Q. Mucio Scaevola consulibus de Dalmatia triumphatum est

topic: The consul Cato fights disgracefully against the Scordisci
quote_la: C. Cato consul Scordiscis intulit bellum ignominioseque pugnavit

topic: Cato's entire army intercepted by the Scordisci in Thrace
quote_la: omnino totus interceptus exercitus quem duxerat Cato

topic: Calpurnius Bestia, bribed by Jugurtha, makes a shameful peace
quote_la: Missus adversus eum consul Calpurnius Bestia, corruptus regis pecunia, pacem cum eo flagitiosissimam fecit, quae a senatu improbata est

topic: Jugurtha buys peace from Bestia with gold
quote_la: Primus in Numidiam Calpurnium Bestia consul inmittitur; sed rex peritus fortius adversus Romanos aurum esse quam ferrum, pacem emit

topic: Metellus defeats Jugurtha in several battles and ravages Numidia
quote_la: Iugurtham variis proeliis vicit, elephantos eius occidit vel cepit, multas civitates ipsius in deditionem cepit

topic: Metellus takes up the war to avenge Roman honour
quote_la: Tandem in ultionem non tam imperii Romani quam pudoris Metellus adsurgit

topic: Bocchus betrays Jugurtha to Sulla, Marius' quaestor
quote_la: capto Iugurtha per quaestorem suum Cornelium Sullam, ingentem virum, tradente Boccho Iugurtham qui pro eo ante pugnaverat

topic: Bocchus purchases Roman friendship with the surrender of Jugurtha
quote_la: Qui ubi diffisus rebus suis alienae cladis accessio fieri timet, pretium foederis atque amicitiae regem facit

topic: Jugurtha led in chains before Marius' chariot and strangled in prison
quote_la: Ante currum tamen Marii Iugurtha cum duobus filiis ductus est catenatus et mox iussu consulis in carcere strangulatus est

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXVIII (Bellum Cimbricum Teutonicum Tigurinum)
topic: Silanus, Manlius and Caepio successively routed by the Cimbri
quote_la: Sed nec primum impetum barbarorum Silanus, nec secundum Mallius, nec tertium Caepio sustinere potuerunt

topic: The consuls Manlius and Caepio destroyed by the Cimbri near the Rhone
quote_la: M. Manlius et Q. Caepio a Cimbris et Teutonis et Tugurinis et Ambronibus, quae erant Germanorum et Gallorum gentes, victi sunt iuxta flumen Rhodanum

topic: Marius annihilates the Teutones, killing 200,000 and capturing their king Teutobodus
quote_la: Cum Cimbris itaque conflixit et duobus proeliis CC milia hostium cecidit, LXXX milia cepit et ducem eorum Teutobodum

topic: Marius and Catulus destroy the Cimbri: 140,000 slain, 60,000 captured
quote_la: Nam proelio, quod simul ambo gesserunt, CXL milia aut in pugna aut in fuga caesa sunt, LX milia capta

locus_hint: liber I, cap. XXXVIII (Bellum Cimbricum Teutonicum Tigurinum)
topic: Marius overtakes the Teutones at Aquae Sextiae
quote_la: prioresque Teutonas sub ipsis Alpium radicibus adsecutus in loco quem Aquas Sextiam vocant

topic: Saturninus wins the tribunate by murdering his rival Ninnius
quote_la: Occiso palam comitiis A. Ninnio competitore tribunatus subrogare conatus est in eius locum C. Gracchum, hominem sine tribu

topic: Saturninus beaten to death by the people after seizing the Capitol
quote_la: Ibi eum facta inruptione populus fustibus saxisque coopertum in ipsa quoque morte laceravit

topic: Cyrene bequeathed to Rome by the testament of king Apion
quote_la: Libya quoque Romano imperio per testamentum Appionis, qui rex eius fuerat, accessit, in qua inclutae urbes erant Berenice, Ptolomais, Cyrene

topic: Drusus rouses plebs and allies with promises of land and citizenship
quote_la: plebem ad se Gracchanis legibus, isdemque socios ad plebem spe civitatis erexit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. VI (Bellum adversus socios)
topic: The Social War explodes at Asculum with the massacre of Romans at the games
quote_la: Asculo furor omnis erupit, in ipsa quidem ludorum frequentia trucidatis qui tunc aderat ab urbe legatis

topic: The Picentes, Marsi and Paeligni begin the Italian war
quote_la: in Italia gravissimum bellum Picentes, Marsi Pelignique moverunt

topic: The consul Rutilius and Caepio fall in the Social War
quote_la: P. Rutilius consul in eo occisus est, Caepio, nobilis iuvenis, Porcius Cato, alius consul

locus_hint: liber II, cap. VI (Bellum adversus socios)
topic: The armies of Rutilius and Caepio routed by the Italians
quote_la: Fusae Rutili copiae, fusae Caepionis

topic: Marius and Pompeius Strabo fight successfully against the allies
quote_la: A Romanis bene contra eos pugnatum est a C. Mario, qui sexies consul fuerat, et a Cn. Pompeio

topic: Sulla destroys Cluentius' army with the loss of a single man
quote_la: ita Cluentium, hostium ducem, cum magnis copiis fudit, ut ex suis unum amitteret

locus_hint: liber II, cap. VI (Bellum adversus socios)
topic: Roman commanders subdue the rebel peoples one by one, Sulla the Samnites
quote_la: adgressique singulos populos Cato discutit Etruscos, Gabinius Marsos, Carbo Lucanos, Sulla Samnites

locus_hint: liber II, cap. VI (Bellum adversus socios)
topic: Pompeius Strabo ends the slaughter with the destruction of Asculum
quote_la: Strabo vero Pompeius omnia flammis ferroque populatus non prius finem caedium fecit, quam Asculi eversione

topic: Sulla marches armed into Rome, kills Sulpicius and drives out Marius
quote_la: Primus urbem Romam armatus ingressus est, Sulpicium interfecit, Marium fugavit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: Sulla turns his legions on Rome through the Esquiline and Colline gates
quote_la: statim Sulla legiones circumegit, dilatoque Mithridate Esquilina Collinaque porta geminum urbi agmen infudit

topic: Mithridates orders all Roman citizens in Asia killed in one day
quote_la: per omnem Asiam litteras misit, ut ubicumque inventi essent cives Romani, uno die occiderentur

topic: Mithridates' edict for the massacre of Roman citizens in Asia
quote_la: cum omnes qui in Asia forent Romanae civitatis homines interfici iussit

topic: Marius and Cinna renew war in Italy against the Sullan order
quote_la: Marius, qui fugatus erat, et Cornelius Cinna, unus ex consulibus, bellum in Italia reparaverunt

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: Cinna, driven from Rome, flees to the Marian party
quote_la: profugus patria sua Cinna confugit ad partes

topic: Marius and Cinna enter Rome and butcher the leading senators
quote_la: ingressi urbem Romam nobilissimos e senatu et consulares viros interfecerunt

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: Heads of the consul Octavius and the orator Antonius displayed
quote_la: Octavi consilis caput pro rostris exponitur, Antoni consularis in Mari ipsius mensis

topic: Sulla besieges Archelaus at the Piraeus and captures Athens
quote_la: Sulla Archelaum apud Piraeum, non longe ab Athenis, obsedit, ipsas Athenas cepit

topic: Sulla starves besieged Athens into submission
quote_la: Primumque Athenas urbem—quis crederet?—frugum parentem, obsidione ac fame ad humanos cibos compulit

topic: Sulla destroys Archelaus' vast army in Boeotia
quote_la: Postea commisso proelio contra Archelaum ita eum vicit, ut ex CXX milibus vix decem Archelao superessent

topic: The king's forces scattered at Chaeronea and Orchomenus
quote_la: omnis copias uno apud Chaeroniam, apud Orchomenon altero bello dissipavit

topic: Sulla concludes peace with Mithridates to hurry to the civil war
quote_la: Pax inter eos ordinata est, ut Sulla ad bellum civile festinans a tergo periculum non haberet

topic: Sulla defeats Norbanus near Capua and receives Scipio's army in surrender
quote_la: Inde etiam ad Scipionem se convertit et ante proelium totum eius exercitum sine sanguine in deditionem accepit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: First clash at Capua by the Volturnus; Norbanus routed, Scipio's troops won over
quote_la: Primum apud Capuam sub amne Volturno signa concurrunt, et statim Norbani fusus exercitus, statim omnes Scipionis copiae ostentata spe pacis oppressae

topic: The younger Marius and Carbo made consuls
quote_la: cum Romae mutati consules essent, Marius, Marii filius, ac Papirius Carbo consulatum accepissent

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: The pontifex Scaevola cut down at the altar of Vesta
quote_la: nam Mucius Scaevola pontifex Vestalis amplexus aras tantum non eodem igne sepelitur

topic: Sulla routs the younger Marius and besieges him in Praeneste
quote_la: Sulla contra Marium iuniorem dimicavit et XV milibus eius occisis CCCC de suis perdidit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: The Marian forces destroyed at Sacriportus and the Colline Gate
quote_la: Apud Sacriportum Collinamque portam debellatae omnes hostium copiae; ibi Marius, hic Telesinus oppressi

topic: Sulla's desperate battle at the Colline Gate against the Marian leaders
quote_la: Rursus pugnam gravissimam habuit contra Lamponium et Carinatem, duces partis Marianae, ad portam Collinam

locus_hint: liber II, cap. IX (Bellum civile Marianum)
topic: Sulla massacres thousands of surrendered men in the Villa Publica
quote_la: Quattuor milia deditorum inermium civium in Villa Publica interfici iussit

topic: Carbo flees to Sicily and is killed there by Pompey
quote_la: Cn. quoque Carbo, consul alter, ab Arimino ad Siciliam fugit et ibi per Cn. Pompeium interfectus est

topic: Pompey, aged twenty-four, triumphs from Africa after killing Domitius and the Numidian king
quote_la: Transgressus inde ad Africam, Domitium, Marianae partis ducem, et Hiardam, regem Mauritaniae, qui Domitio auxilium ferebat, occidit

topic: Sertorius raises a great war in Spain; Domitius killed by Hirtuleius
quote_la: A Sertorii duce Hirtuleio Domitius occisus est

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XI (Bellum civile sub Lepido)
topic: Lepidus driven from Italy by Catulus, dies in Sardinia
quote_la: retro pulsus hostisque a senatu iudicatus incruenta fuga Etruriam, inde Sardiniam recessit, ibique morbo et paenitentia interiit

topic: Pompey sent to Spain against Sertorius alongside Metellus
quote_la: cum inpar pugnae solus Metellus putaretur, Cn. Pompeius ad Hispanias missus est

topic: Drawn battles between the commanders at Lauro and the Sucro
quote_la: ipsi duces comminus invicem experti apud Lauronem atque Sucronem aequavere clades

topic: Nicomedes of Bithynia bequeaths his kingdom to Rome
quote_la: mortuus est Nicomedes, rex Bithyniae, et per testamentum populum Romanum fecit heredem

topic: Cotta defeated by Mithridates and besieged at Chalcedon
quote_la: Cotta apud Chalcedonem victus ab eo acie, etiam intra oppidum coactus est et obsessus

topic: Servilius storms Phaselis, Olympus and the Isaurian strongholds
quote_la: validissimas urbes eorum et diutina praeda abundantes, Phaselin et Olympon evertit Isaurosque ipsam arcem Ciliciae

topic: Lucullus' first campaign destroys vast numbers of the king's troops
quote_la: Ita una hieme et aestate a Lucullo ad centum fere milia regis extincta sunt

topic: Lucullus besieges the besieger, destroying Mithridates' army at Cyzicus by famine
quote_la: Ac dum Mithridates in obsidione Cyzici commoratur, ipse eum a tergo obsedit fameque consumpsit et multis proeliis vicit

topic: Seventy-four gladiators under Spartacus break out of the school at Capua
quote_la: Septuaginta enim et quattuor gladiatores ducibus Spartaco, Crixo et Oenomao effracto Capuae ludo fugerunt

topic: Spartacus, Crixus and Oenomaus escape from Lentulus' gladiatorial school
quote_la: Spartacus, Crixus, Oenomaus effracto Lentuli ludo cum triginta aut amplius eiusdem fortunae viris europe Capua

topic: Spartacus defeats both consuls and gathers an army of sixty thousand
quote_la: duobus simul Romanorum consulibus victis sexaginta fere milium armatorum exercitum congregaverunt

topic: Sertorius murdered by his own men in the eighth year of the war
quote_la: Octavo demum anno per suos occisus est, et finis ei bello datus per Cn. Pompeium adulescentem

topic: Crassus defeats the slave army in Apulia
quote_la: victique sunt in Apulia a M. Licinio Crasso pro consule

topic: Marcus Antonius' overconfident Cretan expedition ends in disaster
quote_la: Primus invasit insulam Marcus Antonius, cum ingenti quidem victoriae spe atque fiducia, adeo ut pluris catenas in navibus quam arma portaret

topic: Crassus restores Roman honour against Spartacus
quote_la: pudoremque Romanum Licinius Crassus adseruit

topic: Lucullus takes Tigranocerta and routs Tigranes' huge army
quote_la: Tigranocertam, civitatem Arzanenae, nobilissimam regni Armeniaci, cepit

topic: Metellus subdues Crete within three years and is styled Creticus
quote_la: Ad id missus Q. Caecilius Metellus ingentibus proeliis intra triennium omnem provinciam cepit appellatusque est Creticus

topic: Pompey's squadrons sweep the pirates from every sea
quote_la: Sic per omnis aequoris portus, sinus, latebras, recessus, promunturia, freta, paeninsulas quidquid piratarum fuit quadam indagine inclusum et oppressum est

topic: The Mithridatic command conferred on Pompey
quote_la: Mox ei delatum etiam bellum contra regem Mithridatem et Tigranem

topic: Pompey defeats Mithridates in a night battle in Lesser Armenia
quote_la: Quo suscepto Mithridatem in Armenia minore nocturno proelio vicit, castra diripuit, quadraginta milia eius occidit

topic: Tigranes surrenders, laying his diadem in Pompey's hands
quote_la: ac diadema suum, cum procubuisset ad genua Pompeii, in manibus ipsius conlocavit

topic: The night battle against Mithridates fought by moonlight
quote_la: Nocturna ea dimicatio fuit et luna in partibus

topic: Mithridates, betrayed by Pharnaces, fails with poison and dies by the sword
quote_la: Sed defectione civium Pharnacisque fili scelere praeventus male temptatum veneno spiritum ferro expulit

topic: Pompey takes Jerusalem in the third month
quote_la: Inde ad Iudaeam transgressus est, Hierosolyma, caput gentis, tertio mense cepit

topic: Catiline's conspiracy exposed; Cicero expels him and his accomplices are strangled
quote_la: A Cicerone urbe expulsus est. Socii eius deprehensi in carcere strangulati sunt

topic: Catiline defeated in battle and killed by the consul Antonius' army
quote_la: Ab Antonio, altero consule, Catilina ipse victus proelio est et interfectus

topic: Catiline crushed by Antonius' army as he marches from Etruria
quote_la: infestis ab Etruria signis patriam petens obvio Antonii exercitu opprimitur

topic: Caesar's first victory over the Helvetii
quote_la: Is primus vicit Helvetios, qui nunc Sequani appellantur

topic: Caesar's first German war undertaken for the complaining Haedui
quote_la: Et prima contra Germanos illius pugna iustissimis quidem ex causis: Haedui de incursionibus eorum querebantur

topic: Caesar invades Britain, unknown before to Roman arms
quote_la: Britannis mox bellum intulit, quibus ante eum ne nomen quidem Romanorum cognitum erat

topic: Caesar crosses to Britain with astonishing speed
quote_la: Classe igitur comparata Britanniam transit mira celeritate

topic: Crassus defeated at Carrhae against the omens and killed with his son
quote_la: cum circa Carras contra omen et auspicia dimicasset, a Surena, Orodis regis duce, victus ad postremum interfectus est cum filio

topic: Surenas' cavalry appears as Crassus' doomed army reaches Carrhae
quote_la: Itaque vixdum venerat Carrhas, cum undique praefecti regis Silaces et Surenas ostendere signa

topic: The legates Cotta and Titurius Sabinus lost to Ambiorix' ambush
quote_la: et castra direpta sunt et Aurunculeium Cottam cum Titurio Sabino legatos amisimus

topic: Vercingetorix unites the Gallic peoples in the great revolt
quote_la: omnis pariter Arvernos atque Biturigas, Carnuntas simul Sequanosque contraxit corpore, armis spirituque terribilis, nomine etiam quasi ad terrorem composito, Vercingetorix

topic: Caesar's one defeat in person among the Arverni (Gergovia)
quote_la: Inter tot successus ter male pugnavit, apud Arvernos semel praesens et absens in Germania bis

topic: Caesar storms Avaricum and reduces Alesia
quote_la: Tum ipsa capita belli adgressus urbes, Avaricum cum quadraginta milibus propugnantium sustulit, Alesiam ducentorum quinquaginta milium iuventute subnixam flammis adaequavit

topic: Caesar marches from Ariminum against his country
quote_la: Propter quam iniuriam ab Arimino, ubi milites congregatos habebat, adversum patriam cum exercitu venit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: The war opens at Ariminum; Domitius driven from Corfinium
quote_la: Prima Arimino signa cecinerunt. Tum pulsus Etruria Libo, Vmbria, Thermus. Domitius Corfinio

topic: Caesar defeats Afranius, Petreius and Varro in Spain
quote_la: Ibi Pompeii exercitus validissimos et fortissimos cum tribus ducibus, L. Afranio, M. Petreio, M. Varrone, superavit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: Massilia dares to shut its gates against Caesar
quote_la: ad Hispanienses Pompei exercitus transeunti per eam duci portas claudere ausa Massilia est

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: Campaign against Petreius and Afranius encamped at Ilerda
quote_la: cum legatis Gnaei pompei, Petreio et Afranio, quos Ilerdae castra habentes apud Sicorim amnem opsidere et ab oppido intercludere adgreditur

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: The vain assault on impregnable Dyrrachium
quote_la: nunc expugnatione Dyrrachi inrita, quippe quam vel situs inexpugnabilem faceret

topic: The decisive battle joined at Pharsalus in Thessaly
quote_la: Deinde in Thessalia apud Palaeopharsalum productis utrimque ingentibus copiis dimicaverunt

topic: Pompey murdered in Egypt; his head and ring sent to Caesar
quote_la: Qui fortunam magis quam amicitiam secutus occidit Pompeium, caput eius et anulum Caesari misit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: Ptolemy seals his treaty with Caesar with Pompey's severed head
quote_la: cum Ptolemaeus, rex Alexandriae, summum civilis belli scelus peregisset et foedus amicitiae cum Caesare medio Pompei capite sanxisset

topic: Ptolemy perishes in the Nile, his body found in golden armour
quote_la: Victus in Nilo periit inventumque est corpus eius cum lorica aurea

topic: Pharnaces, Mithridates' son, defeated in a single swift campaign
quote_la: rebellantem in Ponto et multas populi Romani provincias occupantem vicit acie, postea ad mortem coegit

topic: Caesar victorious in Africa; Cato, Scipio, Petreius and Juba kill themselves
quote_la: Contra hos commisso proelio, post multas dimicationes victor fuit Caesar. Cato, Scipio, Petreius, Iuba ipsi se occiderunt

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: The African war fought even more fiercely than Pharsalia, ending at Thapsus
quote_la: Nihil ergo inter Pharsaliam et Thapson, nisi quod amplior eoque acrior Caesareanorum impetus fuit

topic: At Munda Caesar is nearly beaten and contemplates death
quote_la: ultimum apud Mundam civitatem, in quo adeo Caesar paene victus est, ut fugientibus suis se voluerit occidere

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIII (Bellum civile Caesaris et Pompei)
topic: Munda, the last and most anxious of Caesar's battles
quote_la: Omnium postrema certaminum Munda. Hic non pro cetera felicitate, sed anceps et diu triste proelium

topic: Caesar assassinated in the senate with twenty-three wounds
quote_la: Ergo Caesar, cum senatus die inter ceteros venisset ad curiam, tribus et viginti vulneribus confossus est

topic: Young Octavian, Caesar's testamentary heir, takes his name
quote_la: Octavianus, adulescens annos X et VIII natus, Caesaris nepos, quem ille testamento heredem reliquerat et nomen suum ferre iusserat

topic: Antony, furious at being passed over in Caesar's will, moves against Octavian
quote_la: Prima civilium motuum causa testamentum Caesaris fuit, cuius secundus heres Antonius, praelatum sibi Octavium furens

topic: Antony besieges Decimus Brutus in Cisalpine Gaul
quote_la: Et iam parato exercitu in Cisalpina Gallia resistentem motibus suis Decimum Brutum obsidebat

topic: Antony defeated at Mutina, but both victorious consuls die
quote_la: Qui profecti contra Antonium tres duces vicerunt eum. Evenit tamen ut victores consules ambo morerentur

topic: Octavian relieves Mutina and strips Antony of his camp
quote_la: obsidione Mutinae liberat Brutum, Antonium exuit castris

topic: The triumvirs proscribe the senate; Cicero among the slain
quote_la: Senatum proscripsit, cum Antonio ac Lepido rem publicam armis tenere coepit. Per hos etiam Cicero orator occisus est multique alii nobiles

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVI (Bellum Perusinum. Triumviratus)
topic: Cicero's severed head displayed on the rostra
quote_la: civitas lacrimas tenere non potuit, cum recisum Ciceronis caput illis suis rostris videretur

topic: Brutus and Cassius hold the armies of Macedonia and the East
quote_la: Erant enim per Macedoniam et Orientem multi exercitus, quos occupaverant

topic: Sextus Pompeius raises a great war in Sicily
quote_la: Interim a Sex. Pompeio, Cn. Pompeii Magni filio, ingens bellum in Sicilia commotum est

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVIII (Bellum cum Sexto Pompeio)
topic: Sextus Pompeius holds Sicily and Sardinia with the remnants and armed slave-gangs
quote_la: contractisque infelicis belli reliquiis, cum insuper ergastula armasset, Siciliam Sardiniamque habebat

topic: At Philippi Cassius perishes in the first battle, Brutus in the second
quote_la: Apud Philippos, Macedoniae urbem, contra eos pugnaverunt. Primo proelio victi sunt Antonius et Caesar, periit tamen dux nobilitatis Cassius

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVII (Bellum Cassi et Bruti)
topic: Brutus dies by offering his side to a companion's sword
quote_la: ipse quoque uni comitum suorum confodiendum praebuit latus

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVI (Bellum Perusinum. Triumviratus)
topic: The division of lands to veterans kindles a new war
quote_la: Alterum bellum concitavit agrorum divisio, quod Caesar veteranis patris pretium militiae persolvebat

topic: Lucius Antonius stirs civil war in Italy
quote_la: Sed in Italia L. Antonius consul bellum civile commovit

topic: Lucius Antonius defeated and captured at Perusia but spared
quote_la: Is apud Perusium, Tusciae civitatem, victus et captus est, neque occisus

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVI (Bellum Perusinum. Triumviratus)
topic: Octavian starves Lucius Antonius into surrender within Perusia's walls
quote_la: Caesar adgressus intra Perusiae morus redegit compulitque ad extrema deditionis turpi et nihil non experta fame

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XIX (Bellum Parthicum sub Ventidio)
topic: The Parthians under Pacorus overrun Antony's garrisons; Saxa perishes
quote_la: Et illi Pacoro, duce, regio iuvene, dispulerant Antoniana praesidia; Saxa legatus ne veniret in potestatem a gladio impetravit

topic: Ventidius defeats the Parthian invaders of Syria in three battles
quote_la: L. Ventidius Bassus inrumpentes in Syriam Persas tribus proeliis vicit

topic: Ventidius kills Pacorus on the anniversary of Carrhae
quote_la: Pacorum, regis Orodis filium, interfecit eo ipso die, quo olim Orodes, Persarum rex, per ducem Surenam Crassum occiderat

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVIII (Bellum cum Sexto Pompeio)
topic: The Lucrine lake turned into a harbour for training the fleet against Sextus
quote_la: interciso Herculanae viae limite refossisque litoribus, Lucrinus lacus mutatus in portum

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XVIII (Bellum cum Sexto Pompeio)
topic: Sextus Pompeius finally crushed in the Sicilian strait
quote_la: in illa aquarum quiete classis exercita petitus in Siculo freto iuvenis oppressus est

topic: Antony wins his first Parthian battles but retreats ruined by famine and plague
quote_la: Contra Persas etiam ipse pugnavit. Primis eos proeliis vicit, regrediens tamen fame et pestilentia laboravit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XX (Bellum Parthicum sub Antonio)
topic: Parthian arrows bury two of Antony's legions
quote_la: velut nimbus erupit et missis undique sagittis duas legiones operuerunt

topic: Sextus Pompeius breaks the peace, is defeated at sea and killed in Asia
quote_la: Interim Pompeius pacem rupit et navali proelio victus fugiens ad Asiam interfectus est

topic: Octavian leads the Illyrian expedition in person, first across the bridge
quote_la: In hos expeditionem ipse sumpsit fierique pontes imperavit

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XXI (Bellum cum Antonio et Cleopatra)
topic: Octavian crosses from Brundisium and rings the Actian coast
quote_la: Ad primam novorum motuum famam Caesar a Brundisio traiecerat, ut venienti bello occurreret

topic: Antony, ruled by Cleopatra, launches the great civil war
quote_la: Hic quoque ingens bellum civile commovit cogente uxore Cleopatra, regina Aegypti, dum cupiditate muliebri optat etiam in urbe regnare

topic: Antony beaten in the famous sea battle at Actium
quote_la: Victus est ab Augusto navali pugna clara et inlustri apud Actium, qui locus in Epiro est

topic: Cleopatra dies by the asp's venom
quote_la: Cleopatra sibi aspidem admisit et veneno eius extincta est

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XXI (Bellum cum Antonio et Cleopatra)
topic: The queen leads the flight with her golden stern and purple sails
quote_la: Prima dux fugae regina cum aurea puppe veloque purpureo

topic: Marcus Crassus' campaign against the savage Moesi
quote_la: Accepit omen Marcus Crassus. Illi statim ante aciem inmolato equo concepere votum

locus_hint: liber II, cap. XXXIII (Bellum Cantabricum et Asturicum)
topic: Augustus in person encircles Cantabria with a threefold army from Segisama
quote_la: Ipse venit Segisamam, castra posuit; inde tripertito exercitu totam Cantabriam amplexus

topic: Augustus' conquests include Cantabria and the Alpine Salassi
quote_la: Cantabriam, Dalmatiam saepe ante victam, sed penitus tunc subactam, Pannoniam, Aquitaniam, Illyricum, Raetiam, Vindelicos et Salassos in Alpibus

topic: The Alpine peoples, including the Vindelici, pacified through Drusus
quote_la: sed omnes illius cardinis populos, Breunos, Vcennos atque Vindelicos, per privignum suum Claudium Drusum perpacavit

topic: Drusus subdues the Usipetes and overruns the Tencteri and Chatti
quote_la: Missus in eam provinciam Drusus primos domuit Vsipetes, inde Tencteros percucurrit et Catthos

topic: Drusus attacks the mighty Cherusci, Suebi and Sugambri
quote_la: Inde validissimas nationes Cheruscos Suebosque et Sicambros pariter adgressus est

topic: The Thracians of Rhoemetalces subdued by Piso
quote_la: Ille barbaros et signis militaribus et disciplina, armis etiam Romanis adsueverat; sed a Pisone perdomiti

topic: The Parthians return the standards taken from Crassus
quote_la: Reddiderunt etiam signa Romana, quae Crasso victo ademerant

topic: The Pannonian war waged through Tiberius as the German through Drusus
quote_la: Hoc tamen bellum per Drusum, privignum suum, administravit, sicut per Tiberium, privignum alterum, Pannonicum

topic: On Drusus' death in Germany the senate grants him the name Germanicus
quote_la: defuncto ibi fortissimo iuvene, ipse, quod numquam alias, senatus cognomen ex provincia dedit
